items.heading: DarkCloud
items.text: Dark Cloud Cover A bearish reversal pattern that continues the uptrend with a long white body. The next day opens at a new high, then closes below the midpoint of the body of the first day.

items.heading: EveningStar
items.text: Evening Star A bearish reversal pattern that continues an uptrend with a long white body day followed by a gapped up small body day, then a down close with the close below the midpoint of the first day.

items.heading: HammerHanging
items.text: Hammer Hammer candlesticks form when a security moves significantly lower after the open but rallies to close well above the intraday low. The resulting candlestick looks like a square lollipop with a long stick. If this candlestick forms during a decline, it is called a Hammer. Hanging Man Hanging Man candlesticks form when a security moves significantly lower after the open but rallies to close well above the intraday low. The resulting candlestick looks like a square lollipop with a long stick. If this candlestick forms during an advance, it is called a Hanging Man.

items.heading: InvertedHammer
items.text: Inverted Hammer A one-day bullish reversal pattern. In a downtrend, the open is lower, then it trades higher, but closes near its open, therefore looking like an inverted lollipop.

items.heading: MorningStar
items.text: Morning Star A three-day bullish reversal pattern consisting of three candlesticks—a long-bodied black candle extending the current downtrend, a short middle candle that gapped down on the open, and a long-bodied white candle that gapped up on the open and closed above the midpoint of the body of the first day.

items.heading: Piercing
items.text: Piercing Line A bullish two-day reversal pattern. The first day, in a downtrend, is a long black day. The next day opens at a new low, then closes above the midpoint of the body of the first day.

items.heading: ShootingStar
items.text: Shooting Star A single-day pattern that can appear in an uptrend. It opens higher, trades much higher, and then closes near its open. It looks just like the Inverted Hammer, except it's bearish.
